_about: Intake for the person map: at most 15 plain-language questions (ENGINE_SPEC.md §4). Every question is about the person (about: self). Only free-text answers are evidence. Questions avoid the texts' labels and the diagnosis layer's cue words, so answers are the person's words, not echoes of ours (mapping_rules.intake.question_echo). No question asks for health, diet, name, contact details, location or date of birth (collect only what the reading needs). All but age are optional; a reading needs at least 25 of the person's own words (reading gate).

questions.purpose: Adults only (18+). Under 18: the reading is politely declined before anything else happens. Stored only as a number.

questions.text: What brings you here? Say it in your own words, as you would to a friend.
questions.purpose: The person's own framing of the pattern; the widest unit, for any marker.

questions.text: Think of a recent day when this was strongest. What happened, what went through your mind, and what did you do next?
questions.purpose: One concrete episode: it gives the details, frequency and consequences the specificity rule needs (F1–F3), for any marker.

questions.text: When something you enjoy comes to an end — a show, a trip, a good conversation — what happens in you afterwards?
questions.purpose: Lets the markers of wanting a remembered pleasure again be noticed (rāga YS 2.7; sensual desire as a hindrance; Jain greed). Food is deliberately not among the examples.

questions.text: When someone gets in your way or lets you down, what do you usually do, and how long does it stay with you?
questions.purpose: Markers of aversion and anger: dveṣa (YS 2.8), ill will as a hindrance, Jain anger (krodha), the Gītā's anger born of frustrated desire; duration gives F1.

questions.text: When you sit down to something that needs your attention — work, study, prayer or quiet sitting — what tends to happen?
questions.purpose: Markers of the wandering mind (BhG 6.26, 6.34), restlessness, heaviness and drowsiness in a study or contemplative setting (the one setting where the mapping rules allow those words), and the YS 1.30 obstacles.

questions.text: What does your mind keep going back to, and when does that happen?
questions.purpose: Markers of restlessness and remorse (uddhacca-kukkucca), and of the mind returning to its objects; the 'when' gives F1/F2.

questions.text: When you have to choose, or commit to one path, what happens?
questions.purpose: Markers of doubt and wavering (vicikicchā; saṃśaya among the YS 1.30 obstacles; BhG 4.40).

questions.text: What happens in you when your work goes unnoticed, or when someone else does better than you?
questions.purpose: Markers of pride and I-making (asmitā YS 2.6; conceit, māna; Jain pride) and of envy.

questions.text: Is there something that matters to you that you keep putting off? What happens when you try to begin?
questions.purpose: Markers of the YS 1.30 obstacles of sloth, carelessness and not keeping at it, and of the Gītā's tāmasa signs of rising (BhG 14.8, 14.13) — read only as signs of a guṇa rising, never as a nature.

questions.text: Is there anything you hold on to — a thing, a role, a person, a way things should be — that is hard to let go of? What happens when it is threatened?
questions.purpose: Markers of attachment and grasping (upādāna; rāga; Jain greed) and of the Gītā's 'mine-ness' (mamatā).

questions.text: Are there times when you show others something different from what you really think or want? When?
questions.purpose: Markers of deceit and concealment (Jain māyā, TS 8.9; the Buddhist deceit and hypocrisy, māyā and sāṭheyya).

questions.text: When, even briefly, do you feel most settled or at ease?
questions.purpose: The person's own ground for practice: it lets the pathway start where the person already finds some quiet; it can also provide counter-evidence.

questions.text: Have you already tried something for this — a practice, a prayer, a routine? How did it go?
questions.purpose: Practice experience and stage (for the pathway), and a reported lessening with practice (stored as reported_change, never as a state label).

questions.text: Is there anything else you would like the reading to take into account?
questions.purpose: Anything the questions missed. It is also screened by the safety rules like every answer.
